unreg:knockout_method_of_victory.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before reading the record: (1) regulation goal rates for both finalists from opponent-adjusted strength, with the venue effect set per final (usually neutral, but a host nation or a club playing in its own city is possible); (2) P(level after 90+stoppage), driven by the strength gap and the total goal rate, with low-score dependence and knockout caution that inflate draws, about 25-35% for close finals; (3) extra time: 30 minutes at a reduced rate shaped by fatigue (rest days, accumulated season load, heat at a July World Cup final), the extra substitution and the bench; about 55-60% of level matches go to penalties; (4) shootout close to 50/50, with goalkeeper and taker effects heavily shrunk; (5) contract: regulation includes stoppage time, MOF is either team and MOV is the named team, a fair price applies after cancellation, and no source is named. Required inputs: strength ratings, low-score dependence, knockout draw multiplier, ET rate, bench depth, rest/load, heat, shootout skill, XI/injuries, venue tilt, rules flags. Compared with the record, the chain matches. Differences: the record declares rest/load a GAP even though soc.rest_travel and soc.congestion_load exist; it ignores heat (soc.weather); it treats every final as neutral; and it stacks four overlapping draw/ET calibration inputs. All quotes were checked verbatim against the rules samples (6/6).

findings.text: situational_schedule_motivation is marked GAP ('Rest days before the final and the different end-of-season load ... are not captured') although the catalog already has soc.rest_travel and soc.congestion_load. The record's own mechanism (s3: ET intensity is 'fatigue- and substitute-dependent') needs them. Add both to catalog_entry.inputs, not only to unresolved u2.

environment covers only soc.neutral_final_venue_split. Heat and humidity at a July World Cup final (2026 finals in North American summer afternoons) plausibly lower the ET scoring rate and raise the penalty share, which is the exact channel between the ET and Penalty legs. soc.weather (in the catalog) is missing from inputs, stages and interactions.

Several inputs measure the same thing. soc.knockout_cagey_factor (draw multiplier), the new soc.late_level_risk_appetite (late-level caution), soc.method_path_tree_calibration (empirical phase frequencies) and soc.extra_time_shootout_model plus the new soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate are all fitted on the same historical knockout data and are all labelled primary. Late caution is part of what the cagey multiplier measures, and the phase tree is a calibration target, not an independent input. Without a stated hierarchy (one structural model, one calibration check) the input list invites double counting of draw mass.

soc.home_advantage is audited WEAK because 'Finals are at neutral venues'. That is false in general: a host nation can reach the World Cup final, and a club can play a UCL or UEL final in its home city (e.g. Bayern 2012). The venue input should handle a real home side, not only a crowd split.

The soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate measurement pools 'all knockout matches that went to extra time ... and top domestic cups'. That includes second legs of two-legged ties, where extra time follows a level aggregate rather than a level match, so the game state and incentives differ. Restrict the sample to single-match ties or add a covariate.
soc.added_time is used in stage s5 and in officiating_rules coverage but is absent from catalog_entry.inputs and input_audit.

The interaction between soc.late_level_risk_appetite and soc.penalty_shootout_skill (a manager 'plays for penalties' when his shootout record is perceived as better) is speculative. Without evidence it is a hypothesis, not a mapped interaction.

FBref lost its Opta advanced-stats feed on 2026-01-20 (Sports Reference announcement: xG, shot-creating actions and other advanced stats were removed). The record still lists FBref as the free source for xG and the 'FBref/StatsBomb open data event files' behind soc.late_level_risk_appetite and soc.xg_adjusted_ratings (required_data 'Team strength and lineup data before the final': xg_for, xg_against from FBref free_scrape). FBref does not expose these fields for current data any more; a replacement (FotMob/Opta, Understat for the big-5 leagues, a paid Opta/StatsBomb feed) and a check of whether historical xG stays available are needed. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED until checked.

unreg:match_combo_parlay.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before reading the record: P(YES) = sum over first-goal minute t of P(Argentina scores first at t) x P(Messi on the pitch at t and is the scorer, including penalty and free-kick duty, not an own goal) x P(Argentina advances | leads from t). Advancement must cover an equaliser followed by ET and a shootout, so the ET/shootout model and the knockout draw/caution multiplier are needed. A 0-0 after 120 is NO even if Argentina wins on penalties. Messi's start and withdrawal minute (age 39, minutes management) cut the scorer leg. Penalty-award rate and VAR feed the penalty route. Contract hazards: own goal first (presumably NO), DNP (no void clause; presumably NO), postponement and source unstated, rules_secondary empty. Compared with the record, the mechanism matches. Differences: the record's catalog_entry omits inputs its own stages need (shootout model, cagey factor, penalty rate); it leaves the minutes-management GAP open although soc.player_minutes_expectation exists; and it lists a simulation output as a primary input. Quotes verbatim (2/2).

findings.text: Stages use soc.extra_time_shootout_model (s3: an advancement path after an equaliser), soc.knockout_cagey_factor (s1: the goalless-120 point mass that kills the scorer leg), soc.penalty_rate (s2: the penalty route to the first goal) and soc.var_intervention_rate (s5). None of these are in catalog_entry.inputs or input_audit, so the catalog input list relied on downstream is missing core drivers of both legs.

situational_schedule_motivation is a GAP ('no input estimates tournament-specific minutes restriction'), but soc.player_minutes_expectation ('Expected minutes and rotation risk for a player') already exists and is the natural carrier. It is not referenced, and the planned withdrawal minute is the dominant scorer-leg variable for a 39-year-old. Add it, with a tournament or veteran conditioning in its measurement.

soc.combo_leg_conditional_dependence is defined as the output of a 50k-run joint simulation (dependence ratio, P(B|A)). That is the model's prediction, not an observable input, yet it is labelled primary. It should be a modelling component or validation target, not part of the input list.

soc.lead_protection_knockout_conversion (empirical P(advance | first goal minute, gap)) overlaps soc.tie_advancement_state_tree plus soc.trailing_team_response_hazard, which the record keeps as primary and secondary. Name one as structural and one as calibration to avoid counting the equaliser risk twice.

The interaction soc.penalty_taker_status x soc.var_intervention_rate (multiplicative) is not a real interaction for one match. The tournament VAR penalty rate is a near-constant scalar on the penalty route, already inside soc.penalty_rate.

soc.first_goal_hazard is indexed pregame_knowable 'no' (an in-play hazard) but is used as a primary pregame input. Its pregame form (opening-period scoring rate from ratings) should be stated explicitly.

FBref lost its Opta advanced-stats feed on 2026-01-20 (Sports Reference announcement: xG, shot-creating actions and other advanced stats were removed). The record still lists FBref as the free source for player npxg and shots (required_data 'Player minutes, shots and penalty duty': FBref free_scrape, and 'Team strength and referee/VAR rates': FBref team xG). FBref does not expose these fields for current data any more; a replacement (FotMob/Opta, Understat for the big-5 leagues, a paid Opta/StatsBomb feed) and a check of whether historical xG stays available are needed. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED until checked.

unreg:player_appearance_selection.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before reading the record: gates are (1) eligibility (contract and registration for club windows; federation eligibility AND a call-up to the national-team squad for country windows); (2) fitness per match day (return-to-play for injured players, new-injury and suspension hazard for fit ones); (3) selection into the matchday squad and XI (coach role, rotation in dead rubbers, for example a group finale after qualification); (4) bench entry given score state and substitutions left; (5) window contracts are a union over qualifying fixtures with persistent fitness; the pair contract needs overlapping on-pitch intervals. Contract hazards: 'plays' is undefined for the Balogun and Rodman contracts (minimum minutes, friendlies); the Messi contract requires official playing time; the pair contract counts official matches only; KXPLAYWC is a squad-list contract that belongs with squad selection. Compared with the record, the gate structure and the KXPLAYWC mis-mapping note match. Differences: the record misreads the Balogun window as friendlies only (it spans the USA's home World Cup matches), it has no national-team call-up or squad-selection gate, and it does not use group-stage dead-rubber state. Quotes verbatim (6/6).

findings.text: variants_and_edge_cases says 'USA pre-World Cup matches in that window were friendlies'. The KXBALOGUNPLAY window ('before Jul 7, 2026') also contains the USA's home World Cup group matches (from Jun 12) and the knockout rounds up to the round of 16. That changes soc.window_qualifying_fixture_count (official tournament matches, conditional on USA survival) and makes the friendlies ambiguity matter less.

There is no national-team call-up or final-squad gate. For KXBALOGUNPLAY the player must first be in the USA camp or the 26-man World Cup squad, which is a coach selection with its own drivers (call-up history, positional competition, deadline and replacement rules). Those inputs exist only in the sibling archetype (soc.national_team_call_up_history, soc.positional_slot_competition, soc.squad_list_deadline_and_replacement_rules) and are absent here. s1 lists only club-type registration inputs.

KXPLAYWC is correctly flagged under series_mapping_issues as belonging to unreg:player_squad_selection_and_lineup. However, catalog_entry.contract_types still lists 'Player World Cup' and the target still says 'named in a squad'. The catalog entry should drop it so the two archetypes do not overlap.

For KXWCPLAY (Jordan vs Argentina, Jun 27, the third group match) the main rotation driver is whether Argentina has already qualified or secured first place. soc.group_stage_scenarios exists in the catalog but is not used; soc.stakes_leverage is generic.

The interaction soc.registration_and_league_eligibility x soc.season_minutes_survival_curve ('the gates multiply') is a sequential product of probabilities, which is the mechanism itself, not an interaction between inputs that a feature contrast would test.

The injury source 'Premier Injuries (EPL)' does not cover any sampled subject (Real Madrid, USA, NWSL). Transfermarkt injury records for NWSL players are sparse, so soc.return_to_play_timeline for the Rodman contract depends on own capture. Disclose this as DATA_UNAVAILABLE or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
soc.formation and soc.transfers are used in stages s1 and s5 and in opponent_matchup coverage but are missing from catalog_entry.inputs and input_audit.

Basic minutes and lineups probably remain on FBref after the January 2026 Opta removal, but the record's reliance on 'FBref match logs (minutes)' for soc.pair_onpitch_overlap_model should be confirmed. Transfermarkt match sheets (substitution minutes) are the safer source.

unreg:player_squad_selection_and_lineup.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before reading the record. Final squad: (1) candidate pool from call-ups under the current coach; (2) positional quota ranking among rivals; (3) club form, minutes and fitness approaching the deadline, which are the main movers for fringe candidates such as MLS-based USA players and for veterans' sharpness; (4) injury at the deadline; veteran intent; (5) post-list replacement path (before the first match per KXWCSQUAD; whether goalkeeper replacements later in the tournament count is unstated); (6) leaks and announcements. Starting XI: fitness, suspensions from card accumulation, stakes (third-place match, dead rubbers), opponent system, confirmed XI at T-60, warm-up withdrawal; a non-occurrence by Jul 20 resolves NO. Compared with the record, the structure matches and the settlement claims are correct (KXWCSTART non-occurrence resolves NO, withdrawals after selection stay YES, provisional lists excluded). Differences: there is no club-level form or minutes input, KXPLAYWC is not absorbed, manager-change and replacement edge cases are thin. Quotes verbatim (6/6).

findings.text: There is no club-level form, minutes or fitness input. The summary claims call-up history 'dominates club form', but for fringe candidates (the KXWCSQUAD USA list) and veterans (Ronaldo, Messi) recent club minutes and match sharpness are a primary selection signal and the leading indicator of call-up changes. soc.player_minutes_expectation or soc.congestion_load (club minutes) should be in catalog_entry.inputs, and club match logs should be in required_data. soc.positional_slot_competition mentions 'minutes' without saying whether club or international.
The KXPLAYWC series (same final-squad contract) is not listed in this archetype's series or coverage even though the sibling record maps it here.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard is used in stage s1 and in an interaction but is missing from catalog_entry.inputs and input_audit.

Edge case not disclosed: FIFA tournament rules allow some replacements (notably injured goalkeepers) after the first match. KXWCSQUAD only states that additions 'prior to their team's first match' resolve YES, so a later addition is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS. This is not in unresolved.

soc.national_team_call_up_history uses 'whether named in the latest provisional list'. FIFA does not publish provisional lists and many federations do not either, so this field is likely unavailable for most candidates. Flag it as SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.

Starting-XI stakes for group finales would be better served by soc.group_stage_scenarios (qualification state) than the generic soc.stakes_leverage. Within-tournament player load (soc.congestion_load) is missing from the rotation stage.

unreg:team_win_streak.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written before reading the record: P(at least one run of 5 consecutive wins in the remaining counted matches | current run state) by a Markov chain over ordered per-match win probabilities (opponent, venue, lineup and congestion; cup ties against weaker opponents raise p). Draws break runs. Shared strength drift (injuries, manager change, transfer window) creates positive dependence. The probability is strongly convex in p. Contract hazards: whether a shootout win counts as a win, whether friendlies count, how a run straddling Jan 1 is treated, and a ticker suffix '27' against a rules year of 2026 on an active market as of Nov 2026 (the event may really be the 2027 window, in which case there is no World Cup gap and the sequence differs). Compared with the record, the structure matches. I recomputed the convexity claims under independence: 20 matches give 0.100 at p=0.40, 0.164 at p=0.45 and 0.356 at p=0.55, all correct. Differences: an IRRELEVANT input left in, unlisted stage inputs, a category misuse, and source issues. None changes the core input list. Quotes verbatim (2/2).

findings.text: soc.points_total_distribution is audited IRRELEVANT but is still in catalog_entry.inputs (role context). Remove it.

soc.congestion_load (s2 and situational coverage) and soc.extra_time_shootout_model (s5, officiating coverage, interaction) are used but absent from catalog_entry.inputs and input_audit. Also, shootout classification is a settlement-scope question and does not belong under officiating_rules.

soc.latent_form_persistence (primary) overlaps soc.ratings_uncertainty, soc.manager_dismissal_hazard and soc.season_boundary_strength_reset, which already produce block-level strength drift. Residual serial correlation beyond drift is small in the literature, so labelling it primary risks double-counting the clustering uplift.

The mechanism text is pinned to calendar 2026 ('second half of 2025-26 ... summer break that includes the World Cup', 'roughly 35-50' matches). On 2026-11-07 the market is active with ticker suffix -27, so either most of the 2026 window has passed (and soc.current_win_run_state dominates) or the event is the 2027 window. The record flags the mismatch but does not condition the fixture-count claims on it.

soc.current_win_run_state lists football-data.co.uk as a free source, but the record's own required_data note says it has 'League results; cups not included'. An all-competitions run state needs worldfootball.net or the club's results pages.

FBref lost its Opta advanced-stats feed on 2026-01-20 (Sports Reference announcement: xG and other advanced stats were removed). The record still lists FBref as the free source for team xG (required_data 'Team strength, injuries and managerial events': FBref free_scrape for xg_for/xg_against feeding soc.xg_adjusted_ratings). FBref no longer exposes these fields for current data; a replacement (FotMob/Opta, Understat for the big-5 leagues, a paid feed) and a check of historical availability are needed. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED until checked. Elo from clubelo.com remains a free fallback, so this does not block the input list.
